citations.title: Do We Still Need GraphRAG? Benchmarking RAG and GraphRAG for Agentic Search Systems
citations.excerpt:
Summary:
The paper asks whether agentic search can reduce the need for explicit GraphRAG by evaluating dense RAG and GraphRAG within agentic, multi-round retrieval. It introduces RAGSearch, a unified benchmark that treats dense RAG and graph-based RAG as alternative retrieval backbones in the RAG paradigm and assesses them under agentic inference with standardized protocols (same LLM backbone, retrieval budgets, and inference procedures) across training-free and training-based settings on multiple QA benchmarks. Key findings: agentic search substantially improves dense RAG performance and narrows the gap to GraphRAG, especially in reinforcement-learning–based settings; however, GraphRAG remains advantageous for complex multi-hop reasoning and offers more stable agentic behavior when its offline cost is amortized. The work clarifies the complementary roles of explicit graph structure versus agentic search and provides practical guidance for retrieval design in modern agentic RAG systems. The authors also provide a public benchmark and evaluation code at the linked GitHub repository.

citations.title: How Much Reasoning Do Retrieval-Augmented Models Add beyond LLMs? A Benchmarking Framework for Multi-Hop Inference over Hybrid Knowledge
citations.excerpt:
Summary:
- Paper investigates how much extra reasoning retrieval-augmented models (RAG) contribute beyond base LLMs when solving multi-hop, knowledge-intensive tasks.
- Introduces HybridRAG-Bench, an automated benchmarking framework to evaluate retrieval-heavy, multi-hop reasoning over hybrid knowledge (unstructured text + structured knowledge graphs).
- Four-stage pipeline:
  1) Collect time-framed arXiv corpora as external knowledge sources based on topic filters/times.
  2) Build hybrid knowledge environments with aligned unstructured text chunks and KG graphs for document retrieval and graph traversal.
  3) Generate diverse QA pairs grounded in explicit reasoning paths, including single-hop, multi-hop, hard multi-hop, conditional, counterfactual, and open-ended questions.
  4) Automated quality control to ensure answerability, independence from phrasing, and non-redundancy.
- Key finding (RQ3): Structured knowledge complements text-based retrieval. Hybrid KG-RAG models (text + graphs) outperform text-only RAG across domains, especially on relational, disambiguation, and multi-hop tasks. This indicates structured knowledge provides additive value beyond unstructured retrieval and that the framework is effective for evaluating structured reasoning in KG-RAG systems.
- Platform serves as a testbed to assess how models integrate text and graph evidence and to measure the incremental reasoning added by retrieval components.

Relevance to user query:
- Directly addresses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), evaluation benchmarks, and graph-enabled (hybrid) retrieval approach

citations.title: junhongmit/HybridRAG-Bench
citations.excerpt: HybridRAG-Bench is a reusable benchmark framework to evaluate retrieval-intensive, multi-hop reasoning for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and KG-RAG systems. It automatically builds a unified hybrid knowledge environment from time-framed corpora, combining unstructured text and a linked knowledge graph (Neo4j), then generates diverse reasoning-grounded QA tasks (single-hop to open-ended, including counterfactuals). The pipeline includes: 1) data extraction and alignment of text with graph entities/relations, 2) hybrid knowledge construction (text + KG), 3) reasoning-grounded QA generation validated by an LLM judge, and 4) indexing/reproduction of RAG baselines (LightRAG, GraphRAG, hippoRAG) with configurable caches. The benchmark aims to disentangle retrieval quality from reasoning ability and reveal failure modes hidden in traditional QA benchmarks. Suitable for evaluating how retrieval-augmented methods utilize external knowledge rather than memorization.

citations.excerpt: # Benchmarking Vector, Graph and Hybrid Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Pipelines for Open Radio Access Networks (ORAN). While traditional RAG systems rely on vector-based retrieval, emerging variants such as GraphRAG and Hybrid GraphRAG incorporate knowledge graphs or dual retrieval strategies to support multi-hop reasoning and improve factual grounding. In this study, we conduct a comparative evaluation of Vector RAG, GraphRAG, and Hybrid GraphRAG using ORAN specifications. We assess performance across varying question complexities using established generation metrics: faithfulness, answer relevance, context relevance, and factual correctness. Recent research has proposed Hybrid GraphRAG [5], a unified framework that combines vector-based and graph-based retrieval to leverage the complementary strengths of semantic similarity and structured reasoning. By employing independent generation metrics such as faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance, we provide a more comprehensive and interpretable assessment of system performance [13], particularly in high-. In this work, we present an open, metric-driven comparison of Hybrid GraphRAG, GraphRAG, and Vector RAG pipelines using ORAN specification documents.
